_comment: The ISA scheduling contract, and the one source of every number and rule the two schedulers use.
Edit here, then run: python3 tools/gen_isa_doc.py --write
It generates the tables and the scheduling rules in docs/ISA_AND_INTERFACES.md,
tb/isa_latency_pkg.sv (what the conformance testbenches hold the RTL to) and
tb/isa_schedule.svh (the constants tb/bundle_scheduler.svh schedules with).
asm_constant names board_package/asm.py's copy, checked by gen_isa_doc.py --check; asm.py ships
to boards without this file, so its copies stay written out. A wrong value there reads a
stale register and returns a plausible number without faulting.
"versions" names every ISA version; the top level is the base (v1) and each other version states only its deltas.
tools/check_scheduler_agreement.py holds asm.schedule() and the svh to the same delays.

profile.note: W is the cycle offset at which the op claims the single VREG write port; the earliest dependent consumer is L = W + 1.

operations.issue: II=1; one V op per bundle
II=1; elementwise across two VREGs (vredmax reduces within one). Ordering is vpu_pkg::bf16_gt, the same key the reduction tree uses
II=1; SFU arithmetic includes a multiplier
II=1; W adds the two registered writeback stages to the reduction unit's own latency

operations.vreg_writes: 1 VREG, one result per sublane broadcast across that sublane's lanes
operations.issue: II=1. rb[0] selects sum (0) or max (1); rb is not a register operand, so it creates no dependence. The assembler spells it vlanesum and vlanemax. Taken from a middle level of xlu_reduction_tree, {REDUCE_TAP_SLACK} stages before its 64-wide result
II=1. Four fill a 16x16 tile: beat q takes tile rows 4q..4q+3 from the four sublanes of VREG A. The tile is held in the transpose unit until vtxout

operations.vreg_reads: the staging tile, not a VREG
operations.issue: II=1. Four drain the tile: beat q writes sublane s, lane l from tile[l][4q+s]. W measured by tb_vpu_latency_probe
II=1. VMEM's read latency (vpu_pkg VMEM_READ_LATENCY), then shared writeback staging. Each access holds the VMEM compute port for one cycle (vpu_word_array.sv)
II=1; the only port-C reader outside the M slot, so a bundle may carry a store or a matrix read, not both (isa/slots.json)

Stream engine; {VMATLOAD_ISSUE_INTERVAL} cycles to the next vmatload or vmatpush, 1 to a vmatpop (tb_matrix_command_ii); streams VREG read port C over +1..+{VMATLOAD_PORT_C_LAST}, one weight row a cycle from the last, so VREG base+k is read last at +{VMATLOAD_PORT_C_LAST} - {NUM_SUBLANES}k. Its weights take effect from the next vmatpush. Loads alternate between {MXU_WEIGHT_BANKS} pending weight banks, so it may issue while the tiles before it drain, but no earlier than {MATRIX_WEIGHT_SWITCH_SPAN} cycles after the first vmatpush since the vmatload {MXU_WEIGHT_BANKS} before it

Stream engine; {VMATPUSH_ISSUE_INTERVAL} cycles to the next vmatload or vmatpush, 1 to a vmatpop (tb_matrix_command_ii); streams VREG read port C over +1..+{VMATPUSH_PORT_C_LAST}. First result at +{VMATPUSH_RESULT_LATENCY}; an earlier vmatpop waits for it beat by beat rather than reading a partial result

Pop engine; {VMATPOP_ISSUE_INTERVAL} cycles to the next vmatpop, 1 to a vmatload or vmatpush (tb_matrix_command_ii). The MXU output FIFO carries a whole VREG per entry, so the write port is reserved once, at +{WB_W_MPOP_FIRST}, whatever the stream engine is doing
No SREG scoreboard: a descriptor reading an SREG must issue at least {S_LAT} bundles after the op that writes it. Every op except SMOV_ARG uses the bundle's shared 24-bit IMM

operations.vreg_reads: VMEM, flat word address; no VREG
operations.issue: Issues asynchronously; wait.channel waits for completion. The DESC kind of the MEM slot, so it cannot share a bundle with vld/vst but can with V, M and S. Row count and VMEM address are in words

loop.begin uses the shared 24-bit IMM for {{lo, step, hi}}; loop.begin.r (C opcode {C_OP_LBEGIN_R}) uses it for {{lo, step, skip}} and reads hi at issue from an SREG, which must be written {S_LAT} bundles before, or from a kernel argument, saturated to {LOOP_BOUND_MAX}. hi <= lo runs no trip: nothing is pushed and fetch resumes after the matching loop.end, 3 cycles after the loop.begin.r in simulation. loop.end, wait.channel and halt use no IMM, so they can share a bundle with a scalar immediate. halt waits for DMA to go idle, not for VREG writes in flight: halting with one in flight is a schedule error that simulation asserts and hardware does not catch

rtl_params_asm_constants._comment: asm.py's copy of an rtl_params value that no operation row names (vmatpop's row names only its first beat).

_comment: Timing facts per matrix command, all scheduling inputs; tb_matrix_command_ii measures each.
engine: the M slot has two. vmatload and vmatpush share the stream engine (port C into the MXU input);
vmatpop has the pop engine (MXU output into the VREG write port). A command on one engine may issue
the bundle after a command on the other.
issue_interval: cycles from a command's issue to the next command on the same engine. A stream command
moves one row a cycle from t+1 and retires on its last row, and its engine takes the next command in that
same cycle, so back-to-back commands stream without a gap.
result_latency: cycles from vmatpush to the first vmatpop that finds its result waiting.
A vmatpop issued earlier waits for its result beat by beat, so its writeback lands later than the
calendar booked it: the result latency is a correctness bound, not only a speed one.
vmatpop's interval is not its writeback span; the span is modelled separately, and is one cycle because a FIFO entry is a whole VREG.
The last cycle, counted from issue, in which the command drives VREG read port C.
It streams from t+1 (the controller registers the command), one row a cycle, so a port-C reader
(vst) is legal from t+last+1. Which port it holds is in isa/slots.json.
Each PE switches to the loaded weights as the first activation of the next tile passes it,
so the last PE switches `span` cycles after that tile's first vmatpush. Each PE holds `banks`
pending weight registers and consecutive vmatloads alternate between them, so a vmatload refills
the bank of the vmatload `banks` before it. Issued sooner than `span` after the first vmatpush
since that vmatload, it overwrites weights some PE has not switched to yet.
tb_matrix_weight_pipelining measures the span; tb_matrix_weight_banks runs loads at the stream
engine's spacing, which the banks allow.
Capacities a schedule can exceed. gen_isa_doc.py --check holds asm.py to these;
tb_isa_conformance holds the RTL to each rtl_param.

mxu_output_fifo.note: One per lane (mxu.sv gen_lane_output), counted in result rows: the storage is depth/NUM_SUBLANES entries of NUM_SUBLANES gathered rows, so depth must be a multiple of NUM_SUBLANES. A vmatpush adds NUM_SUBLANES rows and a vmatpop removes as many. Overflow drops results silently; there is no replay.

loop_buffer.note: A longer body refetches from IRAM on every iteration instead of replaying: 2 more cycles per iteration in simulation. Costs time, not correctness; nothing warns.

dma_channels.note: Descriptor channels (minitpu_config_pkg). A descriptor names one and a wait.channel mask holds a bit for each; a channel the RTL does not have never finishes, so a wait naming it hangs.

delay_field.note: One bundle can wait at most 2**width-1 = {MAX_DELAY} cycles, which covers the {VMATPUSH_RESULT_LATENCY}-cycle vmatpush result latency in one bundle. Longer gaps need filler bundles.

scalar.note: A scalar op writes its SREG this many bundles after issue, with no bypass or interlock: a descriptor or a loop.begin.r reading that SREG must issue at least this many bundles later, across a loop back edge too.

_comment: loop.begin.r: its C opcode, the width of the bound the loop frame holds, and how many of them one image may carry.
tb_isa_conformance holds the RTL to the first two; gen_isa_doc.py --check holds asm.py to all three.
Encoding fields widened as HIGH-ORDER extensions: each high bit was spare before, so an image built
against the narrow field decodes to the same value, and a version without the extension has the bit
as spare (zero). gen_isa_doc.py --check holds asm.py to each width and the datasheet holds
sequencer_pkg.sv's default to it. docs/ISA_HEADROOM.md states the rule.

agu_shift_hi.note: The MEM-LDST agu_shift's high bit (3bcf0b7): with it the field is 4 bits and spells a stride of 1 to 2**15 VMEM words; without it, 3 bits and 128 words.

level_sel_hi.note: The loop level's high bit, in MEM-LDST agu_level and the S slot's level: the loop stack holds 2**(2 + bits) loops, 8 with it and 4 without.

_comment: Compiler policy, not ISA: what an LLVM subtarget calls a tuning feature. A version may set one so that
what it compiles is what its users were taught and graded on; the ISA rules above hold either way.
The environment still overrides each one, as its reader says.
compiler_tuning.gemm_pipeline_note: compiler/emit.py gemm_pipelining(): a GEMM's steps placed as one pipelined run (ca41310). MINITPU_CC_GEMM_PIPELINE=on|off overrides.

_comment: The rules asm.schedule() and tb/bundle_scheduler.svh both apply, rendered into the ISA doc.
Names in braces are the published constants ({NAME_NEXT} is the value plus one); the operation and resource notes use them too.
Change a rule in both schedulers and here in one commit; tools/check_scheduler_agreement.py
fails when the two schedulers give any image different delays.
scheduler.intro: `schedule()` in `asm.py` and `tb/bundle_scheduler.svh` implement one model: they walk the bundles in program order, each loop body once, and only raise delay fields; they never reorder. Where a `loop.begin.r` can run no trip they walk every combination of such bodies skipped too, the path skipping all of them first, and repeat until no walk raises a delay. Change a rule in both, and in `isa/latency.json`, in one commit: `tools/check_scheduler_agreement.py` runs both on every kernel image and fails if any delay differs. `asm.pack()`, which does move bundles, keeps the S and M slots in place.
delays: Read after write: a bundle issues no earlier than W + 1 after the producer of any VREG it reads. `vtxout` reads the transpose tile, not a VREG.
Write after write: a bundle issues no earlier than W + 1 after the producer of any VREG it writes, so writes land in program order. sequencer.sv asserts on a write to a VREG still in flight.

Write port: the single VREG write port is booked cycle by cycle; a bundle moves later until none of its write cycles is taken. A `vmatpop` books +{WB_W_MPOP_FIRST} alone, since it writes every sublane together.

Matrix engines: an M command issues no earlier than *t* + interval after the previous command on its engine ({VMATLOAD_ISSUE_INTERVAL} after `vmatload`, {VMATPUSH_ISSUE_INTERVAL} after `vmatpush`, both on the stream engine; {VMATPOP_ISSUE_INTERVAL} after `vmatpop`, on the pop engine). Commands on different engines are ordered only by program order.

Result latency: a `vmatpop` issues no earlier than {VMATPUSH_RESULT_LATENCY} cycles after the oldest `vmatpush` not yet popped. An earlier pop waits for its result beat by beat, so its writes land later than the write port was booked for.
Weight switch: a `vmatload` issues no earlier than {MATRIX_WEIGHT_SWITCH_SPAN} cycles after the first `vmatpush` since the `vmatload` {MXU_WEIGHT_BANKS} before it, whose pending bank it refills.

Port C: a `vst` issues no earlier than the cycle after a `vmatload` or `vmatpush` stops streaming, {VMATLOAD_PORT_C_LAST_NEXT} or {VMATPUSH_PORT_C_LAST_NEXT} cycles after it. A stream command reads port C from the cycle after it issues, so its engine interval alone keeps it off the stream before it.

Matrix read: a bundle that writes a VREG a `vmatload` or `vmatpush` streams lands that write no earlier than the last cycle the stream reads that VREG, so the stream reads the value it was issued against. Rows stream one a cycle from +1, {NUM_SUBLANES} to a VREG: a `vmatpush` reads its VREG through +{VMATPUSH_PORT_C_LAST}, and a `vmatload`, which streams its last row first, reads VREG base+k through +{VMATLOAD_PORT_C_LAST} - {NUM_SUBLANES}k. A `vmatpop` can run beside a stream, so its destination is held to this too; vpu.sv asserts on a write that lands sooner.
Halt: `halt` issues only after every VREG write in flight has landed. The hardware's halt waits only for the DMA to go idle; simulation asserts on a write in flight.

Zero trip: every rule above holds on each path with any combination of `loop.begin.r` bodies removed, since a skipped body lets what follows its `loop.end` issue as soon as the bundle after the `loop.begin.r` would. A gap the skip needs lands on the `loop.begin.r`, paid once per entry, and the taken path keeps it.
A gap longer than one delay field holds ({MAX_DELAY} cycles) is split over empty filler bundles.
refused: Two port-C readers in one bundle (`vst` with `vmatload` or `vmatpush`): the matrix read wins the port and the store writes the wrong register.
Two writes to one VREG in one bundle: they issue together, so no delay orders them.
Two writes in one bundle on one write-port cycle, such as a `vld` (+{WB_W_VLD}) beside a `vmatpop` (+{WB_W_MPOP_FIRST}): they issue together, so no delay separates them.

A `vmatpush` that would leave more than {MXU_OUTPUT_FIFO_DEPTH} results in a lane's output FIFO, counted in program order. `asm.py` runs every loop its trip count, a `loop.begin.r` at 0, 1 and 3 trips; the svh counts each body once. A delay cannot help, because the pops that drain it come later and nothing reorders.

A descriptor beside a control op, two slots claiming the shared immediate, or a MEM kind the decoder does not define: checked when the bundle is built, and again on every word `asm.schedule` is given, since a word OR-ed by hand never passed through the builder (`asm.py` only).

A descriptor, a `loop.begin.r` reading its bound from an SREG, or a scalar op reading its source SREG (`saddi`, `smac`, `sshl`), issued fewer than {S_LAT} bundles after the write to that SREG, counted with any `loop.begin.r` body between them skipped and around loop back edges too (`asm.py` only). A scalar op reading the SREG its own bundle writes reads the old value by definition and is not refused.

A `vmatpop` with no `vmatpush` outstanding, or a `halt` with results never popped, counted over every loop trip as the FIFO is: the first leaves the pop engine armed and the second leaves results for the next launch's first pop, and neither faults (`asm.py` only).
A `vmatload` base above v{VMATLOAD_BASE_MAX}: it streams {VMATLOAD_VREGS} VREGs and the address wraps (`asm.py` only, in the builder and in `schedule`).
More than {MAX_SKIPPABLE_LOOPS} `loop.begin.r` in one image: the walks double with each.
A C opcode the sequencer does not decode: it runs as a nop, silently (`asm.py` only; the svh sees the decoder's nop).
not_modelled: Loop back edges: the walk is straight through, so a hazard carried from the end of a loop body to its start is the kernel's to space. `tools/check_back_edges.py` (in `make host`) replays every image's loops under these rules, each `loop.begin.r` at 0, 1 and 3 trips, and fails on one.

Stalls the walk cannot see: a descriptor's detour through `S_D_WAIT`, `wait.channel`, loop-buffer refetch and a `loop.begin.r` skip's branch make later bundles issue later than modelled in real time, but not in the units' time: every pipeline that carries a result toward the VREG write port, the scalar writeback, VMEM's load delivery and the matrix pop hold through each (ISA-E03, `sequencer.sv`'s issue-time enable), so a write lands W issue cycles after its bundle however long the stall, and the walk's issue cycles are the hardware's. What runs free through a stall (VMEM's array and DMA port, the matrix engines and array) only does so where every rule is a lower bound on distance. `tools/check_issue_stall_freeze.py` (in `tb/run_all.sh`, and with `--board` on silicon) shows it with probes that collide on the machine before ISA-E03.
Which of compute and DMA owns a VMEM region. Scalar-register spacing is refused, never delayed, by the check above.
`vexp` of a positive input (a value, not a schedule; see `AGENTS.md`).

_comment: One target, several subtargets: the top level of this file is the base, which is version v1, and each
version below states only its deltas, as {path: value} into the base (dotted keys; operations[op] picks
the row listing op). compiler/isa/versions.py resolves a version; asm.py carries the same deltas written
out (it ships without this file) and gen_isa_doc.py --check holds every implemented version's constants
to it, version by version. MINITPU_ISA_VERSION, or minitpu-cc --isa, selects one; nothing falls back.
A version whose deltas are null is reserved: named, so a reader refuses it by name, and not implemented.
bitstreams maps each board build_id known to implement a version; run_image.py refuses an image on a bitstream of another version, and on one in no list unless --isa states it.

bitstreams.0xB1E37C21: minitpu e37c210 (the packaged bitstream): one-beat vmatpop, latency 85, 4-bit agu_shift, but the loop stack 4 deep (before 49d895d), so a v1 image nesting five or more loops is wrong there
